item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00207","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C23","C02","C13"],"selected_candidate_label":"C23","confidence":0.97,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C23 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template for the child's central policy explanation. Both texts argue that social-security insurance benefits are inadequate, advocate prompt increases, and explain that rising wages have increased system revenues enough to support higher benefits without impairing the system's finances. The child adapts C23's congressional-policy discussion into a constituent letter and adds an account of the bill's defeat and renewed effort. C02 is a secondary possibility because it shares the constituent-response frame, attacks organized opposition and misleading propaganda, and promises continued efforts to enact legislation, but its underlying policy and details differ. C13 concerns social security and inadequate subsistence payments but advances a materially different veto argument.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"because of the rising wage level, the available revenues of the social security system would permit us to increase the primary benefit rates by an average of five dollars a month without any added cost to anyone","parent_excerpt":"it is now possible to increase these insurance benefits without changing the actuarial status of the old age and survivors insurance system...because the increases in wages which have since taken place will mean a greater increase in the income of the insurance fund than in the liabilities","explanation":"Distinctive shared fiscal rationale: wage growth expands insurance-fund revenues sufficiently to finance higher benefits without undermining actuarial status."},{"child_excerpt":"the insurance payments were inadequate and that they should be raised","parent_excerpt":"If public assistance payments are now to be increased, then old age and survivors insurance benefits should also be increased to at least an equal degree.","explanation":"Both make increased old-age and survivors insurance benefits the operative legislative recommendation."},{"child_excerpt":"It seems only fair that this adjustment in payments should be made for the benefit of those who have already made contributions to the system.","parent_excerpt":"Its purpose is and has always been to supplement our social insurance system...It is essential that a proper relationship be maintained between insurance benefits and assistance payments.","explanation":"The child condenses C23's distinction between contributory insurance and public assistance into an equity argument for contributors."}]}
